papers.title: Optical vortex bullets with large angular momenta
papers.abstract: We investigate three-dimensional spatiotemporal optical vortex solitons (light bullets with a toroidal shape) carrying higher-order orbital angular momentum in Kerr media with anomalous group-velocity dispersion and a transversely localized Gaussian profile of the linear refractive index. Stationary vortex bullets with topological charges (winding numbers) $1\leq \ell \leq 4$ are obtained as numerical solutions of the three-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation, and their existence, structure and stability are systematically analyzed. In terms of atomic Bose-Einstein condensates, these solutions represent matter-wave solitons with embedded vorticity. We examine the dependence of the solution families on the propagation constant, the depth and width of the guiding profile, and $\ell $. It is found that the increase of $\ell $ requires one to use a stronger or wider waveguiding potential to sustain localized states satisfying the Vakhitov-Kolokolov (VK) stability criterion. VK-complying and non-complying branches of vortex-soliton families are separated by a degenerate Townes branch. Direct simulations reveal that, although the guiding profile substantially suppresses the collapse and extends the propagation distance of vortex bullets, their robustness is ultimately limited by azimuthal instabilities, whose growth is enhanced for values of $\ell $. These results demonstrate that engineered refractive-index landscapes significantly enlarge the stability domain of spatiotemporal vortex bullets and provide guidelines for supporting optical bullets carrying large orbital angular momenta.

papers.title: Dispersion of three-dimensional oscillons: a standing-wave perspective
papers.abstract: A spherically symmetric standing wave confined within a finite-radius ball, with weak radiative exchange between its core and boundary, provides a model for an intermediate stage in the adiabatic evolution of the $\phi^4$ oscillon. We employ a multiscale variational framework to derive an approximate description of these standing waves and their energy-frequency relation. The resulting dispersion curve is compared with that obtained from numerical solutions of the boundary value problem for the $\phi^4$ equation on a two dimensional (time and radius) domain. The agreement between the numerical and variational results is excellent near the endpoint of the continuous spectrum but deteriorates as $\omega$ is reduced below $0.85 \omega_0$. We attribute this discrepancy to the growth of the radiation wing, which is neglected in the variational ansatz.

papers.title: Asymptotic breathers in the Manakov system
papers.abstract: We construct vector (two-component) asymptotic Akhmediev breathers in the Manakov system, matching generalized modulational-instability (gMI) eigenmodes to decaying tails of the breather states. The branch-resolved matching provides analytical results linking the gMI-perturbation envelopes to the positions of the emerging breathers. Numerical simulations of the system with the focusing and defocusing nonlinearities corroborate the analytical predictions for each MI branch. We further develop the asymptotic theory for two-breather solutions generated by two independent gMI modes, linking their temporal separation to the input envelopes and interaction-induced shifts. Further numerical simulations reveal that breather patterns exhibit robustness in the presence of weak nonintegrable perturbations. These findings establish a framework relating experimentally controllable input modulations to the branch-selective formation and positioning of breathers in multicomponent nonlinear systems.

papers.title: Hyperparameter Optimization in the Estimation of PDE and Delay-PDE models from data
papers.abstract: We propose an improved method for estimating partial differential equations and delay partial differential equations from data, using Bayesian optimization and the Bayesian information criterion to automatically find suitable hyperparameters for the method itself or for the equations (such as a time-delay). We show that combining time integration into an established model estimation method increases robustness and yields predictive models. Allowing hyperparameters to be optimized as part of the model estimation results in a wider modelling scope. We demonstrate the method's performance on a number of synthetic benchmark problems of different complexity, representing different classes of physical behaviour. This includes the Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard models, as well as different reaction-diffusion systems without and with time-delay. The published version of this preprint can be found under this URL: https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1367-2630/ae2e33 or the DOI: 10.1088/1367-2630/ae2e33

papers.title: Fully localised three-dimensional solitary water waves on Beltrami flows with strong surface tension
papers.abstract: Fully localised three-dimensional solitary waves are steady water waves which are evanescent in every horizontal direction. This paper presents an existence theory for such waves under the assumptions that the relative vorticity and velocity fields are parallel (`Beltrami flows'), that the free surface of the water takes the form $\{z=\eta(x,y)\}$ for some function $\eta: {\mathbb R}^2\rightarrow{\mathbb R}$, and that the influence of surface tension is sufficiently strong. The governing equations are formulated as a single equation for $\eta$, which is then reduced to a perturbation of the KP-I equation. This equation has recently been shown to have a family of nondegenerate localised solutions, and an application of a suitable variant of the implicit-function theorem shows that they persist under perturbations.

papers.title: Quantum vacuum inversion and multi-kink unbinding in the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model
papers.abstract: Quantum fluctuations can unbind a composite soliton while the correction to its mass stays small. We show this beyond perturbation theory for the multi-kinks of the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model. At one loop the vacuum at the centre of the multi-kink becomes the true vacuum at a coupling of order the classical lifting of the vacua. Tensor-network calculations of the lattice theory show that this inversion survives beyond one loop and has a continuum limit, and that the Gaussian effective potential captures it. On finite chains the multi-kink unbinds when the tension of the string of central vacuum between its two halves falls through zero
